name: NT Rappel
designer: Ariel Di Lisio and Aldo Arillo
classification_notes: Curves and diagonals that read strongly at large sizes but keep an active rhythm in text place this as a display-leaning grotesque.
summary: A modern grotesque whose curves and diagonals show off at large sizes while staying dynamic in running text.
description: NT Rappel is built to work at both ends of the scale: its details are pronounced in display use but keep an active, dynamic rhythm in smaller text settings. Five weights with italics and a set of alternate arrows give it reasonable range for branding and editorial work.
foundry_blurb: Nodo describes NT Rappel as a modern Sans Serif whose details are enhanced by large-format use, while smaller formats gain an active and dynamic sense of line and paragraph.

name: NT Neuss
designer: Ariel Di Lisio and Aldo Arillo
classification_notes: A slightly condensed, deliberately anonymous grotesque modelled on generic system fonts places this as a functional grotesque.
summary: A deliberately generic-looking grotesque built as a rebellion against the type world's suspicion of the ordinary.
description: NT Neuss leans into the anonymous look of default system fonts on purpose, arguing that 'generic' needn't mean uninteresting. Slightly condensed proportions give it good performance in running text. Five weights with italics suit complex visual systems and editorial projects.
foundry_blurb: Nodo frames NT Neuss as a rebellion and aesthetic response to design's avoidance of 'generic' and 'ordinary', influenced by anonymous system fonts yet built for complex visual systems and editorial projects.

name: NT Bau
designer: Ariel Di Lisio and Aldo Arillo
classification_notes: A raw, stripped-down structure taking its name from the German word for construction places this as an industrial grotesque.
summary: A raw, stripped-down grotesque named after the German word for construction, built as a neutral base rather than a finished character.
description: NT Bau presents itself as an empty, well-founded structure, Germanic in its stoicism, meant to be furnished and personalised by the projects that use it. Five weights cover the usual range without italics. A monospaced sibling, NT Bau Mono, extends it into technical use.
foundry_blurb: Nodo describes NT Bau as a raw, neutral and stripped-down typeface inspired by the German word 'bau', meaning construction or building, like a well-founded structure ready to be furnished and personalised.

name: NT Bau Mono
designer: Ariel Di Lisio and Aldo Arillo
classification_notes: The fixed-width companion to NT Bau, carrying its raw, industrial character into a monospaced structure.
summary: A neutral monospace with the raw, industrial character of NT Bau, built for typewriter-style prose and code alike.
description: NT Bau Mono keeps its parent family's neutral, construction-inspired forms but fixes the width, suiting both typewriter-style prose and coding environments. Five weights run from Light to Black. A practical, fixed-width extension rather than a distinct design.
foundry_blurb: Nodo describes NT Bau Mono as inheriting the Industrial Revolution's raw qualities, coming in five weights whose monospaced condition comes in handy when creating visual narratives.

name: NT Zeu
designer: Ariel Di Lisio and Aldo Arillo
classification_notes: A reinterpretation of timeless serif conventions with old-style numerals and delicate ligatures places this as a contemporary classic serif.
summary: A contemporary reworking of classic serif conventions, driven by detail rather than novelty.
description: NT Zeu reinterprets timeless, classic serif structures with Nodo's own contemporary twist, adding old-style numerals and delicate ligatures. Three weights with italics give it a rhythmic, detail-driven feel suited to editorial projects, packaging and branding.
foundry_blurb: Nodo describes NT Zeu as a reinterpretation of timeless and classic type redefined by Nodo's distinctive contemporary twist, a family driven by detail with old-style numerals and delicate ligatures.

name: NT Ciceron
designer: Ariel Di Lisio and Aldo Arillo
classification_notes: High contrast between thick and thin strokes with diagonal stress, in the tradition of Didot and Bodoni, places this as a didone display face.
summary: A high-contrast display serif in the tradition of Didot and Bodoni, three years in the making.
description: NT Ciceron pushes stroke contrast to its limit, with diagonal stress that plays thick against thin near the corners of each letter. It's built purely for display sizes rather than text. The foundry describes it as developed over three years across two cities.
foundry_blurb: Nodo describes NT Ciceron as a display typeface inspired by the meticulous and refined heritage of great typography masters such as Didot and Bodoni, showcasing grandiose contrast.

name: NT Dapper
designer: Ariel Di Lisio and Aldo Arillo
classification_notes: Rational, simple forms retrieving late 19th-century origins place this as a neo-grotesque in the classic sense.
summary: A rational neo-grotesque with a full seven-weight range, built for corporate identity and signage work.
description: NT Dapper looks back to the neo-grotesques of the late nineteenth century and updates them with the formal licences of the industrial age. Seven weights with italics and a stylistic alternate set keep the neutral character intact while giving enough range for corporate identity, signage or editorial use.
foundry_blurb: Nodo describes NT Dapper as rational and simple, retrieving its origins from the late nineteenth century, with its neutral character enhanced by alternates in the stylistic set, ideal for corporate identity, signage or editorial use.

name: NT Umami
designer: Ariel Di Lisio and Aldo Arillo
classification_notes: A serif structure with rounded terminations balancing seriousness and playfulness places this as a rounded serif rather than a classic text serif.
summary: A serif with rounded terminations that sits between serious and playful, built for packaging and editorial use.
description: NT Umami softens a serif structure with rounded terminations and delicate stroke modulation, aiming for a dialogue between formality and warmth. Five weights run without italics. Suited to packaging, editorial spreads and communication campaigns.
foundry_blurb: Nodo describes NT Umami as versatile and subtly lively, a serif structure with rounded terminations allowing a dialogue between seriousness and playfulness.

name: NT Stardust
designer: Ariel Di Lisio and Aldo Arillo
classification_notes: Built with geometric shapes reminiscent of code and machinery, this is classified as a monospace with a technical, geometric character.
summary: A geometric monospace with a friendly tech character, built for apps, interfaces and corporate identities.
description: NT Stardust builds its monospaced letterforms from basic geometric shapes, aiming for a contemporary, code-adjacent look without feeling cold. Three weights, no italics. Aimed at corporate identity, advertising and interface work rather than long-form code.
foundry_blurb: Nodo describes NT Stardust as a monospaced typeface constructed with geometric foundations, reminiscent of code and machinery, resulting in friendly tech characters with a contemporary look.

name: NT Voluma
designer: Ariel Di Lisio and Aldo Arillo
classification_notes: Rounded terminals combined with an industrial, mechanical structure place this as a rounded industrial sans rather than a plain grotesque.
summary: An industrial, mechanical sans with rounded ends and a subtly elegant edge.
description: NT Voluma combines elementary, rational forms with rounded terminals for a mechanical face that still carries some elegance. Four weights, no italics, plus a full set of arrow glyphs. Positioned by the foundry for display, editorial and packaging work.
foundry_blurb: Nodo describes NT Voluma as an industrial and mechanical typeface that combines elementary and rational features with a subtly elegant personality, an ideal rounded-end programme for display, editorial or packaging.
